title: Day 51 · Week 7, Day 2 — Physiology: the organ she's growing for someone else — how a grape-sized embryo eats with no blood supply, the plugs that keep the oxygen out until Day 70, the hormone handover, and what spotting means
summary: The fourth Physiology episode, and the placenta's. Your baby is 8–11 mm at Carnegie stage 16, dark-eyed, with a wrist forming; the placenta around it is many times its size and runs ahead of it all trimester. What it is (Burton & Jauniaux 2015: the fetus's lungs, gut, kidneys and liver plus a gland; ~500 g and 12–14 m² of villi at term). The discovery that the seven-week placenta is sealed from the mother's arteries: Hustin & Schaaps 1987 found no intervillous blood flow before 12 weeks in 250 scans, 70 specimens and 3 hysterectomies; electrodes measured placental oxygen under 20 mmHg at 8–10 weeks rising past 50 at 12 (Rodesch 1992; Jauniaux 2000, 2001) — a fifth of adult tissue, by design, to protect organogenesis from free radicals (Burton 2009). What the embryo eats instead: uterine gland secretions, active to week 10, swallowed by the placenta and filtered to the yolk sac, which feeds the gut (Burton 2002; Hempstock 2004; Jauniaux & Gulbis 2000). The valve opening around Day 70, the oxidative burst the placenta prepares for, and the spiral-artery conversion — half a millimetre to 2.5 mm, 2–3 m/s to 10 cm/s — whose failure underlies early pre-eclampsia and growth restriction (Pijnenborg 2006; Burton 2009), and whose premature failure is the common mechanism of miscarriage (Jauniaux, Poston & Burton 2006). The hormone handover from the Day 30 corpus luteum: hCG's jobs (Cole 2010), its peak and 18-week nadir in 443 women (Braunstein 1976), placental GDF15 as the sickness curve (Fejzo 2024), and progesterone and placental lactogen rewiring her appetite (Burton & Fowden 2015). Then spotting: Hasan 2009's 27% from Day 38, and the subchorionic haematoma — one extra loss in 11 in the older bleeding-based literature (Tuuli 2011, 1,735 women) versus no independent association in 2,446 routinely scanned pregnancies once dates and bleeding are adjusted for (Naert 2019, 18.4% prevalence) — with the NHS/ACOG bleeding rule in one line.
action: Ten minutes tonight, two things. One: on the Day 42 index card, add two dates — Day 70, 'the valve opens: maternal blood reaches the placenta, oxygen starts to climb', and Day 84, 'placenta fully running; organ-building done, growth begins'. Two: type the bleeding rule into both phones under the Day 28 after-hours number: any bleeding, call the practice or early pregnancy unit today; severe or one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, faintness, or a pad soaked in an hour, emergency care now. If she has already had spotting this week and hasn't called, make the call together tomorrow morning.
